answers.core: This is a language implementation/syntax feature, so it cannot be implemented in an external library.
answers.workaround: Like I said before, it _is_ possible to achieve something similar with `await get_tree().create_timer(0).timeout` or `await get_tree().process_frame`, but these methods take additional overhead and can unnecessarily slow down program execution. Having this as a language feature would enable a faster way of writing long-running asynchronous functions.

title: Add support for asynchronously awaiting nothing to pause execution for one cycle
